issue:
read_env() method no longer supports returning the path of the loaded .env file

Description

I noticed that in the latest version, the `read_env()` method no longer supports the `return_path` parameter. This parameter was previously used to get the path of the loaded .env file instead of a boolean indicating if the file was loaded successfully.

When trying to use this parameter, I get a TypeError because the parameter has been removed from the method signature.

Here's a simple reproduction script:

```python
from environs import Env

env = Env()
# This used to return the path to the .env file
path = env.read_env(return_path=True)
print(f"Path to .env file: {path}")
```

This code used to work fine in previous versions, returning the path to the .env file as a string, or None if no file was found. Now it fails because the parameter has been removed.
